question: Compare physical and economic water scarcity
expected_answer: Physical water scarcity refers to lack of water resources, while economic water scarcity refers to lack of infrastructure. Examples include the Middle East and Sub-Saharan Africa.
actual_answer: Physical water scarcity occurs when natural water resources are insufficient to meet demand, commonly found in arid regions. Economic water scarcity occurs when water exists but infrastructure or governance is inadequate.

4. Types of Water Scarcity
4.1 Physical Water Scarcity

The global freshwater crisis is a multidimensional challenge involving environmental, economic, and political factors. Sustainable management requires a combination of technological innovation, policy reform, and behavioral change. Without intervention, water scarcity will increasingly constrain economic development, food security, and human health.

Occurs when natural water resources are insufficient to meet demand.

Common in arid regions (e.g., Middle East, North Africa)
4.2 Economic Water Scarcity

Occurs when water exists but infrastructure or governance is inadequate.
